item.title: Hamamatsu Unagi: Japan's Eel Capital on Lake Hamana — Guide
item.description: Hamamatsu is Japan’s unagi (freshwater eel) capital, the brackish waters of neighbouring Lake Hamana having hosted the country’s first commercial eel farming over a century ago, and the city’s restaurants have refined the craft of grilling eel ever since. The classic dish is unagi glazed in a sweet-savoury tare sauce, grilled over charcoal and served on rice, and Hamamatsu sits on the historic boundary between styles, so both the Kanto method (steamed then grilled, meltingly soft) and the Kansai method (grilled straight through, crisp-edged) are served here side by side.
